purpose: Bounded nearest-work comparison for the already selected cubic token-transport theory

records.title: QKSAN: A Quantum Kernel Self-Attention Network
records.scope: Identity; Section3.1 quantum query/key score and Section3.2 conditional link

facts.finding: The score is a squared inner product of separately transformed query/key states.
The score measurement controls an operation on a second value register; deferred and intermediate measurement constructions are compared.

records.difference: The examined score is pairwise query/key fidelity plus measurement-conditioned register operations. The current exact route instead builds a key-key cubic Gram graph, mixes all class-query token amplitudes by its unitary, then squares.
limits: Only identity and listed score/link pages read; other architecture, results, appendices and code uninspected.
No claim that all quantum kernel attention variants are covered.

records.title: Learning with SASQuaTCh: a Novel Variational Quantum Transformer Architecture with Kernel-Based Self-Attention
records.scope: Identity; kernel convolution derivation and SASQuaTCh circuit

facts.finding: Under a stationary-kernel assumption, the attention operation is represented as a convolution evaluated in Fourier space.
The sequence is embedded in quantum registers and processed by QFT, a trainable kernel unitary, inverse QFT and a task-specific readout.

records.difference: This establishes a quantum Fourier-domain kernel architecture. The current generator is an input-dependent cubic token-state Gram graph, with fixed tau and class-query amplitude initialization; the fixed-key coordinate ceiling comparison is a different scoped question.
limits: Listed main-method pages only; experiments, additional figures, appendices and code uninspected.
The paper discusses state-preparation and measurement costs; no speedup or hardware inference is imported.

records.title: Flow-based Spectral Kernel Learning for Nonstationary Attention
records.scope: Identity; nonstationary kernel/RFF/flow equations; projection absorption assumption

facts.finding: A bivariate spectral distribution and normalizing flow parameterize a nonstationary random-feature attention kernel, with a spectral regularizer.
ELU+1 makes the implemented features positive; the paper explicitly limits its unbiasedness theorem to the signed features before this transformation.
Projection absorption assumes uniform density in continuous similarities and does not certify this assumption for the finite implementation.

records.difference: Learning kernel spectra and absorbing query/key projections into an expressive function family differs from a fixed-key physical-query ceiling. Its conditional theorem is not evidence for or against the exact finite cubic mechanism.
limits: Listed method pages only; AppendixA proofs, empirical claims and source code uninspected.
The acquired artifact is an arXiv preprint; conference status is not independently checked.

records.title: Quantum Complex-Valued Self-Attention Model
records.scope: Identity and main complex similarity/CLCU value aggregation; equations20-28 visually inspected

facts.finding: Complex inner-product query/key weights retain amplitude and phase and are used to aggregate value states.
Complex LCU prepares half-phases, applies controlled value unitaries and transpose preparation, then postselects the normalized complex-weighted value sum.
The model combines similarity-weighted value states and additional trainable complex state weights.

records.difference: The inspected attention is complex pairwise query/key weighting followed by coherent value-state aggregation. Our selected candidate instead builds an input-dependent cubic key-key Gram generator, transports token-index amplitudes and then forms probabilities for classical value pooling. This is an architectural distinction, not a theorem separating unrestricted learned families.
interpretations: Complex weights, phase preservation and coherent aggregation are established neighboring components; none is a sufficient novelty claim here.

For unrestricted globally input-dependent orthonormal value states, the identity U s = sum_j s_j U e_j represents token transport as coherent value aggregation. Our fixed-key query-ceiling theorem alone therefore does not exclude such an enlarged value family. This algebraic observation does not show that the inspected finite local value circuits implement that global family.
limits: Only listed identity/main-method pages inspected; experiments, appendices and source code not assessed.
No claim of disjoint function families or exhaustive novelty clearance.
No hardware, learning or task-utility inference imported.

records.title: Robustness of Measurement, discrimination games and accessible information
records.scope: Identity and main measurement robustness/post-processing/discrimination statements; equations on pp2-3 visually checked

facts.finding: Measurement post-processing uses a classical stochastic matrix on effects.

facts.locator: p2 Eq7 and p3 first paragraph
facts.finding: Robustness equals sum of effect operator norms minus one; every rank-one POVM reaches dimension minus one.
Its discrimination advantage is optimized over ensembles against guessing without measurement, not a candidate-versus-native trained task comparison.

records.difference: Native and coherent fixed-key attention can be represented as POVMs. Full-rank unsmoothed effects are rank one for both, so this generic robustness saturates equally and cannot certify their task advantage. A constructed phase pair instead distinguishes particular outcome information, subject to its separate query-state comparator.
limits: Only listed main pages inspected; appendix proofs, experiments and code uninspected.
Naimark representation, measurement resource monotones and constructed discrimination games are established tools, not L5 novelty.
No learned NLP utility, ordering over all ensembles or nearest-neighbor novelty clearance follows.

records.title: Attention-based Deep Multiple Instance Learning
records.scope: Identity, three-stage MIL architecture and attention pooling; p3 Eqs7-8 visually inspected.

facts.finding: The paper separates instance embedding, symmetric pooling and a final bag-level transformation, which may be a neural network.
Attention is a normalized exponential of a local tanh score; pooled embeddings are their weighted sum.

records.difference: With an affine bag logit, this local normalized pooling obeys the same rational-additive condition as our native head. The paper also permits a nonlinear final bag classifier, which our finite-grid certificate does not cover.
limits: Only the listed main-method pages were read; experiments, supplementary proofs and source code were not assessed.
No exhaustive novelty, decision-family separation, quantum necessity, learning or task-utility claim follows.

records.title: Set Transformer: A Framework for Attention-based Permutation-Invariant Neural Networks
records.scope: Identity, local pooling comparison, MAB/SAB/ISAB/PMA definitions and stated invariance/universality; pp3-4 visually inspected.

facts.finding: Set pooling includes nonlinear processing after aggregation; the paper motivates explicit interactions as an architectural and optimization choice.
SAB uses multihead self-attention among set elements; ISAB introduces learned inducing points for O(nm) interaction.

PMA aggregates using learned seeds; the encoder/decoder includes interactions and feedforward transformations. The paper states permutation invariance and universality; the supplementary proof was not read.

records.difference: Cross-element interaction beyond independent local affine pooling is an established design direction. The native-grid theorem neither separates the graph route from Set Transformer nor establishes novelty over interaction-capable set networks.
limits: Only the listed main-method pages were read; experiments, supplementary proofs and source code were not assessed.
No exhaustive novelty, decision-family separation, quantum necessity, learning or task-utility claim follows.

records.title: Diffusion Scattering Transforms on Graphs
records.scope: Identity, diffusion metric and scattering/stability statements; theorem5.3/corollary5.4 visually checked onp7. Proof appendix/code/empirics not assessed.

facts.finding: Defines a lazy diffusion on degree-normalized real undirected graphs and a permutation-aligned graph diffusion metric.

facts.locator: p6 Eq11 and Lemmas5.1-5.2; p7 Theorem5.3/Corollary5.4
facts.finding: Bounds changes of diffusion scattering representations in terms of graph perturbation distance and spectral-gap/depth factors.

records.difference: Graph-propagation stability is established prior theory. Our finite-tau calculation instead compares a normalized Hermitian Born-routing head with a zero-coupled nuisance block, separates explicit Born/EPS query mass from graph perturbation, and propagates a power-affinity contrast into fixed-utility logit/CE/margin bounds. This scoped formulation is not a priority claim or a separation from the general graph-stability literature.
limits: Appendix proofs, code and task experiments not inspected.
The reviewed bound is standard perturbation reasoning applied to this exact interface; no learned robustness, coherence necessity or L5 acceptance follows.

records.title: Bargmann Invariants and Geometric Phases - a Generalised Connection
records.scope: Identity, original Bargmann definition/phase invariance, null-phase motivation; p6 equations visually inspected.

facts.finding: Defines cyclic inner-product products as traces of rank-one projectors, invariant to individual state phases, and connects their phase to geodesic polygons.

records.difference: The same three-state invariant appears in our exact query-conditioned token current, with utility-difference weights and fixed generator normalization. Bargmann geometry itself is established; this mapping is not a priority claim.
limits: Only listed sections read; examples and full generalization proofs in later sections not assessed.
A nonzero geometric phase is neither a task-gain nor a quantum-necessity certificate.

records.title: Quantum Transport Enhancement by Time-Reversal Symmetry Breaking
records.scope: Main text and analytical Methods, including gauge/time-reversal identities; p5 visually inspected. Supplement/code not assessed.

facts.locator: p2 Eq2 and initial-state description; pp4-5 Methods Eq6,8-9
facts.finding: Complex Hermitian hopping gives chiral walks; conjugating a Hamiltonian reverses unitary site transport in time, and diagonal gauge changes preserve localized-site transition probabilities. Loop phase sums are gauge invariants.

records.difference: The inspected work starts at localized site states. Our current is prepared coherently from each class query, and actual RZ-row sign flips conjugate both generator and initial amplitudes while native Born logits stay fixed. Its transport/gauge tools are established neighbors, not new claims.
limits: Site-state phase-removal results do not apply without transforming our coherent initial state too.
No inspected source implies NLP utility, cubic necessity, learned-family separation, or exhaustive novelty clearance.

records.title: Weighted complex projective 2-designs from bases: optimal state determination by orthogonal measurements
records.scope: Listed identity and mathematical sections only; selected equations visually checked.

facts.finding: A projective second-moment design matches the Haar symmetric projector and requires at least d^2 states.
The frame-potential gap equals a squared Hilbert-Schmidt moment mismatch.

records.difference: Conditional cubic-routing nullity is an exact-interface consequence of this established moment identity. Designs, isotropy and the moment-gap identity are not new contributions.
limits: Unlisted sections, proofs, experiments and source code not assessed.
No exhaustive priority clearance or task-utility claim.

records.title: Stronger Welch Bounds and Optimal Approximate k-Designs
records.scope: Listed identity and mathematical sections only; selected equations visually checked.

facts.finding: Moment operators, projective designs and partial transposition encode the mixed-tensor geometry.
The paper gives the full spectrum and invariant-subspace structure of mixed Haar moments rho_n,m; n=2,m=1 is a direct neighbor of the cubic lift.

records.difference: Our earlier Sym^2(C^d) tensor conjugate(C^d) decomposition lies in an established mixed-moment setting. The exact EPS routing consequence differs in interface but has no established substantive novelty. No stronger-Welch optimality result is imported.
limits: Unlisted sections, proofs, experiments and source code not assessed.
No exhaustive priority clearance or task-utility claim.

records.title: Quantum Graph Attention Networks: Trainable Quantum Encoders for Inductive Graph Learning
records.scope: Identity, GAT baseline and complete listed main quantum feature-map/convolution/pooling/readout definitions. p5 Eqs6-10 visually checked.

facts.finding: Trainable neighbor coefficients multiply classical node inputs before unitary feature mapping; neighbor states are tensorized.
A quantum convolution/pooling channel processes the encoded states and observable expectations give classical embeddings.

records.difference: The inspected mechanism weights input features before quantum encoding and uses convolution/pooling/readout. It does not display our input-dependent entrywise-cubic key-Gram Hamiltonian acting on class-query token-index amplitudes followed by Born probabilities for value pooling. This is a scoped construction distinction, not a separation from arbitrary globally conditioned quantum encoders.
limits: Unlisted sections, empirical comparisons, implementation and code not assessed.
Quantum graph attention, data-dependent unitaries and adaptive neighborhood aggregation are established neighboring components.
No exhaustive priority clearance, task superiority, implementation equivalence or new L5 acceptance.

synthesis.candidate_scope: Fixed-key nonlinear amplitude transport: linear-Gram query-null, cubic separation, minimality in a restricted entrywise polynomial family, and a full-rank overcomplete stable witness. The numerical local-family grid explains the native interface limitation; generic cross-token interaction alone is not a central novelty claim.
unresolved: No exhaustive novelty clearance, especially frame/POVM and nonlinear graph-walk theory.
No held-out utility or necessity/mediation claim; formal report pending.
A new combination of familiar ingredients alone is not L5.
Fixed-key query-region separation is not a full learned-family separation from globally conditioned coherent value aggregation; substantive novelty must respect this boundary.
Whole-local-affine-family logit separation does not distinguish interaction-capable Set Transformer or nonlinear bag decoders. Generic cross-token interaction is established prior art.

Nuisance-stability calculation is an exact-interface adaptation of standard tools. Fixed-mask real-state sensitivity does not support a cubic advantage; no central novelty or coherence necessity follows.

Born-invisible finite-circuit conjugation and value-weighted current yield a prospective diagnostic, not novelty or task utility. See current-orientation.md; all four frozen final-trace routes remain necessary controls.

Second-moment nullity is an exact-interface consequence of established design mathematics, with no converse or utility guarantee. The independent informationally complete pure-region lead remains unreviewed and rank-conditional. Neither is L5 clearance; formal report remains pending.

Generic native/cubic pure-region disjointness is unproved: a full-column-rank simple-norm family has a rank-zero coincidence differential. Dimension counting alone is insufficient. No actual-circuit genericity or utility result follows.
